gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two $599 picks are rated on the same 80% basis but at different counts (FOSSiBOT F2400 4,000+ cycles vs Anker F2000 3,000 cycles), or that FOSSiBOT's own runtime formula derates the F2400's 2,048 Wh to about 1,741 Wh deliverable.
standout_why: I could not open any rival page: cheapestwh.com, outletpicks.com, powerstationgearlab.com and our own dealectric.com page all failed in WebFetch with a TLS certificate error, and curl was blocked in this session. The score therefore rests only on the result titles (cheapestwh and outletpicks are titled as $/Wh price comparisons) and on ChatGPT's rendered answer, which carries capacity, watts, price, $/Wh and one warranty and no cycle-retention basis, surge figure or usable Wh. Treat the 2 as provisional until someone reads those pages.
decides: It confirms FOSSiBOT F2400 over Anker F2000 at ChatGPT's equal $599: one third more rated cycles on the same 80% basis, and a 4,800 W surge. The catch is price: fossibot.com sells the F2400 at $669 today, so the under-$600 claim depends on the Amazon listing, which I did not verify. No maker store I checked sells a 2 kWh unit under $600 today; the closest is AFERIY P210 at $602.10, then ECO-WORTHY PS2400 at $759.99 and Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 at $999.

findings.label: Deliverable energy by the maker's own runtime formula
findings.value: about 1,741 Wh of the 2,048 Wh nameplate (0.85 factor)
findings.note: FAQ formula: 'Working time = F2400's Watt-Hours * 0.85 / operating power', with the example 2048Wh*0.85/700w = roughly 2.49 hours; the FAQ calls it theoretical lab data. Arithmetic: 2,048 x 0.85 = 1,740.8 Wh. Per deliverable Wh that is $669 / 1,740.8 = $0.384 at the maker price, or $599 / 1,740.8 = $0.344 at ChatGPT's unverified price, against $0.292 per nameplate Wh in ChatGPT's table.
